bottom_line: In 308 patients with acute decompensated heart failure, there was no significant difference in patients’ global assessment of symptoms with bolus every 12 hours vs continuous infusion (mean AUC, 4236±1440 and 4373±1404, respectively; P = 0.47).
implications: These data support that, over 72 hours, bolus vs continuous infusion did not materially change symptom global assessment (mean AUC 4236±1440 vs 4373±1404; P = 0.47) or mean creatinine change (0.05±0.3 vs 0.07±0.3 mg per deciliter; P = 0.45). For dose strategy, high dose showed more net fluid loss (4899±3479 vs 3575±2635 ml; P = 0.001) and greater weight loss (–8.7±8.5 vs –6.1±9.5 lb; P = 0.01), but also more worsening renal function by creatinine rise >0.3 mg/dl (23% vs 14%; P = 0.04); it does not establish differences in the 60-day clinical composite because no significant difference was observed (hazard ratio with high dose, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.60 to 1.16; P = 0.28).

major_points.text: Prospective, double-blind randomized trial comparing bolus vs continuous infusion and low vs high dose IV furosemide strategies.
major_points.quote: In a prospective, double-blind, randomized trial, we assigned 308 patients with acute decompensated heart failure to receive furosemide administered intravenously by means of either a bolus every 12 hours or continuous infusion and at either a low dose

major_points.text: Coprimary endpoints were symptom global assessment (VAS AUC over 72 hours) and change in serum creatinine from baseline to 72 hours.
major_points.quote: The coprimary end points were patients’ global assessment of symptoms, quantified as the area under the curve (AUC) of the score on a visual-analogue scale over the course of 72 hours, and the change in the serum creatinine level from baseline to 72 hours.

major_points.text: Bolus vs continuous infusion: no significant difference in global symptom assessment.
major_points.quote: there was no significant difference in patients’ global assessment of symptoms (mean AUC, 4236±1440 and 4373±1404, respectively; P = 0.47)

major_points.text: Bolus vs continuous infusion: no significant difference in change in creatinine from baseline to 72 hours.
major_points.quote: mean change in the creatinine level (0.05±0.3 mg per deciliter [4.4±26.5 μmol per liter] and 0.07±0.3 mg per deciliter [6.2±26.5 μmol per liter], respectively; P = 0.45)

major_points.text: High-dose vs low-dose: nonsignificant trend toward better global symptom assessment with high dose.
major_points.quote: a nonsignificant trend toward greater improvement in patients’ global assessment of symptoms in the high-dose group (mean AUC, 4430±1401 vs. 4171±1436; P = 0.06)
